questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to live in Paris, since I love culture and the arts and it has played a significant role in shaping the arts and humanities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some complications with my host university about not getting the classes that I originally wanted but it worked out in the end.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to finde the information needed, however the information came quite late. So I could not prepare very much beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction and intro package to the exchange students. Otherwise I found all the information needed on the website and Sorbonne.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got a room in Cité Universitaire, which I would highly recommend for anyone coming to Paris to study.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Apply to Cité Universitaire, it's much cheaper than other housing off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to be registrated at my host university, and when registrating for classes we just got a google doc to fill out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration for the department helped with finding courses, however they mostly spoke french which was a bit difficult.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get the classes I wanted because there was a technical issue with my registration and all the classes I wanted was full. However the administration helped me find other courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you sign up the classes that you want properly and before the deadling, otherwise there might not be any spots left.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the courses were a bit easier than what I'm used to and there was not as much course work and reading during the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was less lecture and more seminar style classes, which I liked. However, they count class participation as part of your overall grade which I'm not used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Writing the living land (ecocritic perspective on 19th century british literature)
Entangled Artefacts (global history and material culture class)
Other Stories (experimental American literature from the 20th century)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend 'Other Stories' as a class, it was my absolute favourite

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think I spend more on food and going out than I had initially thought I would

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't try any but I was introduced to them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could both join different sports, there was a cinema club and language club and probably many more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't try any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed visiting some of Paris museums, because there are so many and a lot of them are free for European students under 26.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy but it would definitely help if you spoke just a little bit french.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try talking to them in class or join one of the class. I found some of my friends in class settings.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think it really helps you on a daily basis if you know just a little french because at restaurants, bakeries and supermarkets they much prefer french.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and going out culture in France is great and there is so much good food and relatively cheap everywhere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for a room at Fondation Danoise in Cité Universitaire because then you're guaranteed a social environment and friends while you're here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want a really cheap lunch you can eat lunch at their canteen (Crous) for 3,5 euros.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me the most rewarding experience was being able to live and enjoy Paris

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge was the french bureaucracy and how you really have to keep coming back and write a lot of emails for them to do something for you sometimes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
